question: This year, 2026, the three flotilla organisations – Freedom Flotilla, Madleen Thousands, and Sumud Flotilla – will set sail once again with European citizens aboard. Operating in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, they aim to break the Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip, which has been in place since 2007.

They will navigate peacefully in international waters, flying the flags of some EU countries, which, if attacked, would trigger the application of Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union. The EU authorities are aware that Israel has already hijacked numerous ships in the Mediterranean, so this should come as no surprise and steps must be taken to prevent it. U.N.
Security Council Resolution 2803 does not prohibit maritime aid nor relations with the Palestinian population. In view of the above: 1.
What preventive measures will the Commission take to avert Israeli pirate attacks?
What action has it taken against Israel following the attacks in 2025 and before?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.5.2026) The EU shares the aim of delivering urgent humanitarian aid to Gaza and ending the suffering of its civilian population. Since the 7th of October 2023, the EU released over EUR 640 million in humanitarian assistance for Palestine, working with trusted partners to ensure aid reaches those most in need.

The EU calls for the removal of all restrictions obstructing humanitarian access, in line with international humanitarian law (IHL). The EU has continued to urge Israel to ensure unimpeded aid delivery and compliance with IHL. While the EU respects the humanitarian commitment of the flotilla participants, it discourages such initiatives due to the risks to participants’ safety and the potential for escalation.

The freedom of navigation under international law must be upheld, and any use of force against vessels in international waters, including seizures or attacks, is unacceptable. The EU has not received formal requests for assistance from the flotilla organisers, and it has no mandate or assets to escort private vessels.

The EU Member States bear responsibility for consular protection and the security of their citizens at sea. Should incidents occur, the EU stands ready to support affected citizens via the EU Civil Protection Mechanism1, to assist member states with any medical evacuation needs.
